core_obligations: Write [Z]_{k+1} = sum n_i [W_i] over the irreducible components of Z of delta-dimension k + 1, note the family is locally finite, and reduce to the coefficientwise identities [Z_0]_k = sum n_i[(W_i)_0]_k and its analogue at infinity, since the family lemma then gives the rational equivalence (proof lines 3420-3435).

Fix an integral closed Z' of delta-dimension k with generic point xi' and set xi = (xi', 0); let A = O_{X times_S P^1_S, xi} and let I be the ideal cutting out Z, so that A/I = O_{Z,xi} has dimension one by the choice of xi', and use hypothesis (3) to conclude that A/I is Cohen-Macaulay (proof lines 3437-3449).

Use the dimension bound on Z_0 to get dim(A/(t,I)) = 0 for the element t cutting out X times D_0, hence t is a nonzerodivisor on A/I; identify the W_i through xi with the minimal primes q_i over I with multiplicities length_{A_{q_i}}(A/I)_{q_i}, and match n = length_A(A/(t,I)) with m = sum length_A(A/(t,q_i)) length_{A_{q_i}}(A/I)_{q_i} by the additivity lemma (proof lines 3449-3466).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to coefficientwise identities on the two fibres (proof lines 3420-3435).
Move the comparison into the local ring of the product at a point of the fibre and use Cohen-Macaulayness (proof lines 3437-3449).
Use the nonzerodivisor property of the fibre equation and the additivity lemma (proof lines 3449-3466).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the closed-subscheme form of the projective line argument: for a closed Z in X times P^1 of dimension at most k + 1 whose two fibres have dimension at most k and whose embedded points inside those fibres have dimension below k, the two fibre cycle classes are rationally equivalent on X (statement lines 3403-3417, tag 02S5). The proof runs a coefficient comparison in the local ring of the product at the generic point of a component of the fibre, where the absence of embedded points gives that A/I is Cohen-Macaulay and the dimension bound on the fibre makes the fibre equation a nonzerodivisor, after which an additivity statement over the minimal primes over I finishes the count. The local algebra is the substance, so the claim is H2.
